The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed fake, counterfeit, expired, banned, and substandard products worth N100 billion in Ogun State.
The products included medicines, alcoholic beverages, cosmetics and other regulated items considered dangerous to public health.
Officials carried out the destruction exercise on Friday at the Ogwama dumpsite, Ogere Remo, Ogun State.
The agency’s spokesperson, Christiana Obiazikwor, disclosed this in a statement sent to PREMIUM TIMES on Friday.
Speaking at the flag-off ceremony, NAFDAC Director-General, Mojisola Adeyeye, said the exercise aimed at preventing dangerous products from re-entering the Nigerian market.
She said the products included counterfeit, expired, controlled, unregistered, and banned medicines, unwholesome food products, and cosmetics.
Among the items destroyed were banned alcoholic beverages packaged in sachets and PET bottles below 200ml, banned Analgin injections, expired Codeine cough syrups, Oxytocin injections and counterfeit cosmetics.

Ms Adeyeye said, “The estimated street value of these products being destroyed today stands at N100 billion only.”
She explained that the exercise formed part of the agency’s sustained efforts to prevent fake, expired and substandard products from returning to circulation.
The NAFDAC director-general said recent enforcement operations had exposed several illegal manufacturing and distribution networks, particularly in Lagos and Ogun states.
She disclosed that operatives uncovered a warehouse in Lagos originally intended for tools and hardware, where illegal cosmetic products were being manufactured at the building’s penthouse.
Officers also recovered cartons of Augmentin and Ampicillin packets, leaflets, and other unregistered cosmetics.
In another operation, investigators uncovered a production facility where counterfeit versions of popular alcoholic beverage brands were manufactured. Expired energy drinks were also allegedly being revalidated and stored for sale.
The agency further uncovered a residential building allegedly converted into a production and distribution centre for unauthorised and registered herbal mixtures.
Ms Adeyeye said suspects arrested in connection with the activities would face the full weight of the law.
She also disclosed that NAFDAC, working with relevant stakeholders, mopped up more than 100,000 cartons of banned sachet and small PET-bottle alcoholic beverages from manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers across Lagos and Ogun states.
The latest destruction comes amid sustained enforcement against counterfeit products across the country.
In May, PREMIUM TIMES reported that NAFDAC destroyed counterfeit and expired products worth N1.8 billion in Kuje, Abuja. The items included counterfeit medicines and other regulated products.
The destruction followed enforcement operations targeting illegal distribution networks.
Ms Adeyeye commended the Nigeria Customs Service for handing over pharmaceutical products, including cartons of Codeine cough syrup containing codeine, for destruction.
She also acknowledged the support of the Nigeria Police Force, Nigerian Army, State Security Service, Pharmacists Council of Nigeria, National Drug Law Enforcement Agency and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps.
The NAFDAC director-general urged community and religious leaders, health practitioners, the media and members of the public to intensify public education on the dangers of purchasing medicines from unauthorised vendors.
It is imperative that you educate your families and wards about the dangers of patronizing quacks and unauthorised vendors,” she said.
She urged Nigerians to provide useful information to the agency to help identify and eliminate counterfeit, unregistered and dangerous products.
Ms Adeyeye reiterated that NAFDAC remained committed to ensuring that food, drugs, cosmetics, medical devices, chemicals, packaged water and beverages available in Nigeria were safe, wholesome and effective.
